Today, Amazon's subsidiary Ring announced the launch of its first smart door lock. This product addresses a key issue that has troubled many smart lock users: battery drain. Ring has an innovative solution to circumvent this problem, with the product set to launch in the first quarter of 2027. In addition, the company also unveiled several new security cameras with improved low-light performance.

Ring Smart Door Lock

The concept of a smart door lock is nothing new, but Ring aims to address the battery drain issue of smart locks. To prevent you from being locked out at inconvenient times, the Ring Smart Door Lock allows you to turn the thumb turn on the lock a few times to generate enough power to run the lock for a while, so you can then open the door and get back inside.

The Ring Smart Door Lock supports everything you'd expect from a smart door lock. You can unlock it with your fingerprint, a touch keypad, or your phone with the Ring app.

The Ring app also enables several features, including remotely viewing and locking the door, or setting up recurring or time-limited access for family members or other visitors. It also integrates with Amazon Echo as well as other Ring doorbells and cameras you might own.

The lock comes in three colors: black, silver, and bronze, with no additional wiring required. It will go on sale early next year at US$249. You can learn more here.

Brand-New 4K Cameras

In addition to its first smart door lock, Ring has also launched several 4K cameras that support the new Retinal Vision 4K standard. This means you can get excellent image quality and accurate color in low-light conditions. The following products are available for pre-order or purchase starting today:

  • Outdoor Cam 4K Plus: 140° wide field of view, with multiple power options including battery, plug-in, wired, and Power over Ethernet — US$149.99 on Amazon, learn more here
  • Floodlight Cam 4K Plus: powerful floodlights, supports 24/7 continuous recording and smart detection, requires wired connection — US$219.99 on Amazon, learn more here
  • Spotlight Cam 4K Plus: 550-lumen spotlight, 140° wide field of view, available in battery, plug-in, and solar configurations — US$199.99 on Amazon, learn more here
  • Indoor Cam 4K: Ring's first 4K indoor camera, supports dual-band Wi-Fi 6, 115° field of view — US$99.99 on Amazon, learn more here

Ring has also launched a Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K priced at US$69.99, bringing its 360° pan-tilt coverage to a more affordable price point. It can track motion and features a privacy cover. You can learn more here.
